newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Tesco keeps momentum going.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Tesco keeps momentum going.

text.p: British supermarket giant Tesco Plc's first half profits should show further gains when it reports on September 17 but analysts will be keener to see how margins and sales are faring in current competitive conditions.

Analysts are looking for pretax, pre-exceptional profits of 310 to 337 million stg, up from 290 million stg previously, while the dividend payout should be 3.25 to 3.3 pence per share, compared with 3.05 pence.
Tesco indicated at its annual results in April that it would slow dividend growth to reflect that in earnings, prompting estimates for a rise to hover around 6.5 percent or so.
But the focus is likely to be on Tesco's sales and margins as it looks to maintain its leadership position gained at the expense of arch-rival J. Sainsbury last year.
Tesco's sales growth has been helped by its ClubCard loyalty scheme which was launched over a year ago but analysts said now the card's success could present tough year-earlier comparisons.

"Last summer Tesco was trading excellently, with the help of ClubCard and the hot weather. This summer has not been so good and the comparisons could be tougher," said Andrew Kasoulis, analyst at SBC Warburg.
Tesco said in June that like-for-like sales were up seven percent in the first 14 weeks of the current year and analysts will be looking to see if that momentum has continued.
"If Tesco has maintained that sales growth, that will be great, but we are expecting a slowdown later in the year," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

At the same time, margins will be under scrutiny, after Tesco launched its latest "Unbeatable Value" price campaign earlier this month and petrol prices, subjected to a vicious price war, start to stabilise.

"Price is still very critical and we would like to know the impact of Tesco's latest campaign. Petrol seems to have stabilised, so that could enable investment in margins elsewhere," said the analyst.

A fierce price war over petrol between oil majors and supermarkets appears to have cooled, but Tesco said in June that petrol profits for the year would be hit, although it was offsetting the effect elsewhere.
Analysts will also be looking for signs of expansion both in the UK through new store openings and overseas.
Tesco's name was linked earlier this year to the sale of French group Docks de France but it said it ruled a purchase out because it did not consider the deal a viable proposition.
Docks de France finally succumbed to a bid from privately-owned Auchan in July, but analysts felt Tesco might still be persuaded to flex its muscles abroad.
"Tesco should and could make quite a big European acquisition quite soon. Long-term, it would be the right thing for them to do but short-term it would be earnings dilutive," the analyst said.
